subject: Polity
topic: Centre-State Relations I — 7th Schedule, legislative/administrative/financial relations
description: Centre-State relations in the Indian Constitution: 7th Schedule (Union/State/Concurrent Lists), Articles 245-263 (legislative), 256-263 (administrative), Finance Commission (Art 280), Sarkaria Commission — standard IBPS PO/UPSC format.

questions.stem: The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution divides legislative subjects among which three lists?

options.option_text: Union List (List I), State List (List II), and Concurrent List (List III)
Central List, Provincial List, and Residuary List — this is not the constitutional terminology
Federal List, Regional List, and Joint List — terms from some foreign constitutions, not Indian
Exclusive List, Shared List, and Emergency List — no such classification exists in Schedule 7

questions.explanation: 7TH SCHEDULE: contains three lists dividing subjects of legislation. UNION LIST (List I): ~100 subjects on which ONLY Parliament can legislate. Examples: defence, foreign affairs, railways, banking, currency, atomic energy, central taxes. STATE LIST (List II): ~61 subjects on which ONLY State Legislature can legislate (ordinarily). Examples: police, public order, land, agriculture, public health, state taxes. CONCURRENT LIST (List III): ~52 subjects on which BOTH Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate. In case of conflict: Parliament's law prevails. Examples: criminal law, marriage, education (shifted from State to Concurrent by 42nd Amendment 1976), labour. RESIDUARY POWERS: Art 248 — Parliament alone has power to legislate on matters NOT in any list. NUMBERS to remember: approx. 100 Union, 61 State, 52 Concurrent (these change with amendments — don't memorise exact numbers, know the order). ART 246: Parliament = exclusive on List I; State = exclusive on List II; both = List III. PYQ FREQUENCY: 7th Schedule lists in IBPS PO, SSC CGL, UPSC Prelims — extremely commonly asked 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Article 249 of the Indian Constitution allows Parliament to legislate on a State List subject when:

options.option_text: The Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by 2/3 majority declaring it necessary in the national interest
The President issues a proclamation declaring a national emergency under Article 352
The Governor of a state requests the Centre to take over a state subject too
A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament approves the takeover by a simple majority

questions.explanation: ART 249: Parliament may legislate on STATE LIST subjects IF the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution (by 2/3 of members present and voting) declaring it EXPEDIENT IN THE NATIONAL INTEREST. VALIDITY: such a law is valid for 1 year (renewable). SIGNIFICANCE: Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is the protector of state interests — only the upper house (which represents states) can authorise this takeover. DIFFERENT FROM ART 250 (NATIONAL EMERGENCY): during a National Emergency (Art 352), Parliament AUTOMATICALLY gets power to legislate on State List — no RS resolution needed. ART 252: Parliament can legislate on State List if 2 or more states request it (by state legislative resolutions) — the law applies only to those consenting states. ART 253: Parliament can legislate on ANY subject to implement international treaties. ART 246A (101st Amendment, GST): both Parliament and States can levy GST — an additional concurrent power on tax. EXAM TRAP: Art 249 (national interest, RS resolution) vs Art 250 (emergency, no resolution needed) vs Art 252 (states' request). PYQ FREQUENCY: Art 249 mechanism in UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL, state PSC polity 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which Article of the Indian Constitution establishes the Inter-State Council for coordination between the Union and States?

options.option_text: Article 263 — the President may establish such a Council if it appears in the public interest
Article 256 — this deals with the obligation of states to comply with Central laws
Article 280 — this establishes the Finance Commission for Centre-State financial distribution
Article 312 — this deals with creation of All-India Services, not inter-State coordination

questions.explanation: ART 263: The President MAY establish an INTER-STATE COUNCIL if it appears necessary for better co-ordination of policies and actions between Union and States. FUNCTIONS: (1) inquire into and advise on inter-state disputes. (2) investigate and discuss subjects common to Union and States. (3) make recommendations for better co-ordination. ACTUAL ESTABLISHMENT: Inter-State Council established by Presidential Order 1990 (based on Sarkaria Commission recommendation). COMPOSITION: Prime Minister (Chair), Chief Ministers of all states, Administrators of UTs, 6 Union Cabinet Ministers. STANDING COMMITTEE: established under ISC for preparatory work. NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT COUNCIL (NDC): separate body under Planning Commission (now defunct) — both ISC and NDC served coordination functions. PUNCHHI COMMISSION (2007-2010): recommended strengthening the ISC, making it a permanent working body meeting 3× per year. ZONAL COUNCILS: Art 263 can also establish Zonal Councils — 5 Zonal Councils exist (North, South, East, West, Central). PYQ FREQUENCY: Art 263 + Inter-State Council in UPSC Prelims, state PSC 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Article 356 of the Indian Constitution ('President's Rule') allows the Centre to take over state administration when the President is satisfied that:

options.option_text: The constitutional machinery in a state has broken down (governance cannot continue per the Constitution)
The state government has passed legislation conflicting with a Concurrent List central law
The state legislature has not met for more than 6 consecutive months in a financial year
The Governor has lost confidence in the Chief Minister's ability to run the government

questions.explanation: ART 356 (STATE EMERGENCY / PRESIDENT'S RULE): President can assume functions of state government (via Governor's report or otherwise) if CONSTITUTIONAL MACHINERY IN THE STATE HAS FAILED. 'Governance cannot be carried on in accordance with provisions of the Constitution.' DURATION: initially 2 months → approved by Parliament → 6 months at a time → maximum 3 years (with special conditions for years 1-3). EFFECTS: State Legislature dissolved or suspended, Executive (CM+Cabinet) dismissed, Parliament legislates for the state. S.R. BOMMAI CASE (1994): Supreme Court held Art 356 is justiciable (can be reviewed by courts); floor test must precede dismissal; President's proclamation subject to judicial review; if revoked, dissolved legislature can be revived. SARKARIA COMMISSION: recommended strict conditions before invoking Art 356 — exhaust all other options; consult CM first. MISUSE: Art 356 used 125+ times since 1950, often for political reasons — Bommai case significantly curbed this abuse. PYQ FREQUENCY: Art 356 + S.R. Bommai case in UPSC Prelims, IBPS PO, SSC CGL polity — very commonly asked 1-2× per year.

questions.stem: The Finance Commission of India, established under Article 280, makes recommendations on all of the following EXCEPT:

options.option_text: The allocation of funds from the MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act) scheme
Distribution of net proceeds of Union taxes between Centre and States (vertical devolution)
Principles governing grants-in-aid to states from the Consolidated Fund of India
Any other matter referred to it by the President in the interests of sound finance

questions.explanation: FINANCE COMMISSION (Art 280): quasi-judicial body constituted every 5 years by the President. CONSTITUTIONAL MANDATE — recommendations on: (1) VERTICAL DEVOLUTION: distribution of net proceeds of taxes between Union and States. (2) HORIZONTAL DISTRIBUTION: sharing among states. (3) GRANTS-IN-AID (Art 275): to states that need assistance beyond tax share. (4) ANY OTHER MATTER (Art 280(3)(d)): referred by President. 16th FINANCE COMMISSION (2023-28 terms): currently operational. DEVOLUTION SHARE: 16th FC recommended 41% of central taxes to states. NOT UNDER FINANCE COMMISSION: MGNREGA allocations, CSS (Centrally Sponsored Schemes) funding, specific project grants — these are executive decisions of the Union Government, NOT FC recommendations. OPTION B, C, D are all within the FC's mandate. DISTINCTION: FC recommends on the FORMULA for devolution; actual allocation under CSS/MGNREGA is administrative discretion of Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) or Ministry. PYQ FREQUENCY: Art 280 and Finance Commission mandate in UPSC Prelims, IBPS PO, SSC CGL — 1-2× per exam cycle.

questions.stem: The Sarkaria Commission (1983) was specifically constituted to examine:

options.option_text: Centre-State relations — it submitted a 1600-page report in 1988 with 247 recommendations
Electoral reforms — it recommended changes to the voting system and constituency delimitation
Police reforms — it proposed restructuring of the state police under a new constitutional framework
Administrative reforms — it reviewed the bureaucratic structure and All-India Services efficiency

questions.explanation: SARKARIA COMMISSION: constituted in 1983 by the Indira Gandhi government. CHAIRMAN: Justice R.S. Sarkaria (former Supreme Court judge). OBJECTIVE: examine the working of existing arrangements between the Union and States in all spheres including legislative, administrative, and financial relations. REPORT: submitted 1988 — 247 recommendations (accepted 180+ broadly). KEY RECOMMENDATIONS: (1) Art 356 (President's Rule) should be used sparingly as a last resort. (2) Inter-State Council should be set up immediately (done in 1990). (3) Governor should be an eminent person from outside the state, not a political appointee. (4) All-India Services should be maintained and strengthened. (5) Concurrent List should not be expanded further; state autonomy on List II should be respected. (6) Residuary powers of taxation should go to States. PUNCHHI COMMISSION (2007-10): second major Centre-State review under Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi — recommended making ISC a permanent body. UPSC ANGLE: cooperative federalism, NITI Aayog (replaced Planning Commission 2015) promotes this. PYQ FREQUENCY: Sarkaria Commission mandate in UPSC Prelims, state PSC, IBPS PO GA 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Under Article 200 of the Indian Constitution, a Governor may reserve a state bill for the President's consideration. In which of the following situations is reservation MANDATORY (not discretionary)?

options.option_text: When the bill would derogate from the powers of the High Court — the Governor MUST reserve it
When the bill involves expenditure from the state Consolidated Fund above a certain threshold
When the bill has been passed by the state legislature twice after the Governor's first return
When the bill is a money bill and the Governor disagrees with its financial provisions

questions.explanation: ART 200 — GOVERNOR'S OPTIONS with a state bill: (1) ASSENT. (2) WITHHOLD assent. (3) RETURN for reconsideration (if not a money bill). (4) RESERVE for Presidential consideration. MANDATORY RESERVATION (Art 200, proviso): If the bill is one that DEROGATES FROM THE POWERS OF THE HIGH COURT, the Governor SHALL reserve it — no discretion. WHY? High Courts are constitutional bodies; states cannot unilaterally alter their powers — only the Parliament can, through constitutional amendment. OTHER DISCRETIONARY RESERVATION: Governor MAY reserve a bill if it endangers the position of the state High Court or certain other situations where he thinks Presidential assent is warranted. OPTION B: no threshold for expenditure triggers mandatory reservation. OPTION C: if Governor returns a bill and legislature passes it again (with or without amendments), the Governor MUST give assent to that reconsidered bill — but this is about the second-passage rule, not mandatory reservation. OPTION D: money bills cannot be returned or reserved by the Governor (Art 207); Governor must assent or withhold for money bills (no return). UPSC ANGLE: Art 200 vs Art 201 (President's options on reserved bills). The interplay between Centre and state on judicial powers is critical. PYQ FREQUENCY: mandatory reservation under Art 200 in UPSC Prelims, state PSC polity — 1× per 3-4 years, discriminating question.
